description: Linear control systems: transfer function and state-space models, time and frequency responses, Bode, Nyquist, Nichols and root-locus analysis, controllability and observability, regulator and estimator design, and simulation of Modelica system models.

tools.name: TransferFunctionModel
tools.description: Represents a linear system by its transfer function in the Laplace or Z variable, for single- or multi-input systems. It is created from a numerator and denominator, a rational expression, or by converting another model. Most control analysis functions accept it directly.
tools.usage:
TransferFunctionModel[expr, s]
TransferFunctionModel[{num, den}, s]
TransferFunctionModel[ssm]
tools.notes: Add a SamplingPeriod option or use ToDiscreteTimeModel for discrete-time systems.

tools.name: StateSpaceModel
tools.description: Represents a linear system in state-space form with A, B, C and D matrices, in continuous or discrete time. It can also be created by linearizing a nonlinear system of equations about an operating point. State-space form is required for most modern control design functions.
tools.usage:
StateSpaceModel[{a, b, c, d}]
StateSpaceModel[tf]
StateSpaceModel[{eqns, vars, inputs}, {x0}, ...]
tools.notes: StateSpaceModel[nonlinear system] performs Jacobian linearization automatically.

tools.name: OutputResponse
tools.description: Computes the output of a system to a specified input signal over time, symbolically or numerically. Standard test signals such as UnitStep and DiracDelta are commonly used. Use it to simulate step, impulse and arbitrary input responses.
tools.usage:
OutputResponse[sys, u, t]
OutputResponse[sys, u, {t, tmin, tmax}]
tools.example:
tf = TransferFunctionModel[4/(s^2 + s + 4), s];
Plot[Evaluate@OutputResponse[tf, UnitStep[t], {t, 0, 20}], {t, 0, 20}]
tools.notes: StateResponse gives the internal state trajectories instead of the output.

tools.name: StateResponse
tools.description: Computes the state trajectories of a state-space system for a given input and initial condition. It exposes internal behaviour that the output alone hides. Use it to check for state saturation and internal oscillation.
tools.usage:
StateResponse[sys, u, t]
StateResponse[{sys, x0}, u, {t, tmin, tmax}]

tools.name: BodePlot
tools.description: Plots the magnitude and phase of a system's frequency response against frequency on logarithmic axes. Gain and phase margins can be displayed automatically. It is the standard frequency-domain design and stability tool.
tools.usage:
BodePlot[sys]
BodePlot[sys, {wmin, wmax}]
BodePlot[sys, GainPhaseMargins -> True]
tools.example:
tf = TransferFunctionModel[100/(s (s + 5) (s + 20)), s];
BodePlot[tf, GainPhaseMargins -> True, GridLines -> Automatic]

tools.name: NyquistPlot
tools.description: Plots the frequency response in the complex plane as frequency varies, which allows stability to be judged by encirclements of the critical point. It is the graphical form of the Nyquist stability criterion. Use it for systems with delays and non-minimum-phase behaviour.
tools.example:
tf = TransferFunctionModel[1/((s + 1)^3), s];
NyquistPlot[tf, PlotRange -> All]

tools.name: NicholsPlot
tools.description: Plots open-loop gain in decibels against phase in degrees, with optional closed-loop contours. It combines the information of Bode and Nyquist plots in one diagram. Use it for loop-shaping design.

tools.name: RootLocusPlot
tools.description: Plots how the closed-loop poles move in the complex plane as a parameter, usually loop gain, is varied. It shows directly when a system becomes unstable. Use it for classical gain selection and pole placement intuition.

tools.name: SingularValuePlot
tools.description: Plots the singular values of a multi-input multi-output system's frequency response. It generalizes the Bode magnitude plot to MIMO systems, bounding gain in all input directions. Use it for robustness analysis and H-infinity design.

tools.name: TransferFunctionPoles
tools.description: Returns the poles of a transfer function model, the roots of its denominator. Pole locations determine stability and dominant dynamics. Use it together with TransferFunctionZeros for a complete pole-zero picture.

tools.name: TransferFunctionZeros
tools.description: Returns the zeros of a transfer function model, the roots of its numerator. Right-half-plane zeros indicate non-minimum-phase behaviour that limits achievable bandwidth. Use it when diagnosing undershoot and control limitations.

tools.name: ControllabilityMatrix
tools.description: Computes the controllability matrix of a state-space system, whose rank determines whether all states can be driven by the inputs. Rank deficiency identifies uncontrollable modes. Use it before attempting full state feedback design.
tools.notes: ControllableModelQ returns the boolean answer directly.

tools.name: ObservabilityMatrix
tools.description: Computes the observability matrix of a state-space system, whose rank determines whether the internal state can be reconstructed from outputs. It is the dual of the controllability matrix. Use it before designing an observer or Kalman filter.

tools.name: ControllableModelQ
tools.description: Tests whether a state-space model is completely controllable, returning True or False. It is a quick precondition check for pole placement and LQR design. ObservableModelQ is the dual test.

tools.name: ObservableModelQ
tools.description: Tests whether the states of a model can be determined from its outputs, returning True or False. It is required for observer and estimator design to be possible. Use it alongside ControllableModelQ when assessing a plant.

tools.name: StateFeedbackGains
tools.description: Computes state feedback gains that place the closed-loop poles at specified locations. It implements classical pole placement for controllable systems. Use it when you have explicit target dynamics in mind.

tools.name: LQRegulatorGains
tools.description: Computes optimal state-feedback gains that minimize a quadratic cost on states and inputs, the classic LQR problem. The weighting matrices Q and R trade off performance against control effort. Use it when pole locations are less meaningful than an explicit cost.
tools.usage:
LQRegulatorGains[ssm, {q, r}]
LQRegulatorGains[{ssm, inputs}, {q, r, p}]
tools.notes: For a digital controller, convert the plant with ToDiscreteTimeModel first and call DiscreteLQRegulatorGains on the discrete model.

tools.name: LQGRegulator
tools.description: Designs a linear-quadratic-Gaussian controller combining an LQR state feedback with a Kalman estimator. It handles process and measurement noise explicitly. Use it when the state must be estimated from noisy outputs.

tools.name: KalmanEstimator
tools.description: Constructs a Kalman filter state estimator for a system with specified process and measurement noise covariances. The result is a state-space model producing state estimates from inputs and measurements. Use it for sensor fusion and noisy state reconstruction.
tools.notes: EstimatorGains computes just the observer gain matrix for a chosen set of observer poles.

tools.name: EstimatorGains
tools.description: Computes observer gains that place the estimator error poles at specified locations. It is the dual of StateFeedbackGains. Use it to design Luenberger observers with chosen convergence rates.

tools.name: PIDTune
tools.description: Automatically tunes a PID, PI or PD controller for a given plant using a chosen tuning rule or performance criterion. It can return the controller, the closed-loop system or a full design summary. Use it for fast practical controller design.

tools.name: SystemsModelSeriesConnect
tools.description: Connects two systems in series so that the output of the first drives the input of the second. It handles both transfer function and state-space models. Use it to build cascaded plants and controller-plant chains.
tools.notes: SystemsModelParallelConnect sums outputs instead of cascading them.

tools.name: SystemsModelParallelConnect
tools.description: Connects systems in parallel so that they share inputs and their outputs are summed. It is used to model additive paths and disturbance channels. Both model types are supported.

tools.name: SystemsModelFeedbackConnect
tools.description: Closes a feedback loop around a system, optionally through a second system in the feedback path. Negative feedback is the default convention. Use it to form closed-loop models for analysis.

tools.name: SystemsModelStateFeedbackConnect
tools.description: Applies state feedback with given gains to a state-space model, returning the closed-loop system. It pairs directly with StateFeedbackGains and LQRegulatorGains. Use it to verify the resulting dynamics.

tools.name: MinimalStateSpaceModel
tools.description: Removes uncontrollable and unobservable modes from a state-space model, returning a minimal realization of the same input-output behaviour. Smaller models are faster to analyze and better conditioned. Use it after model reduction or interconnection.

tools.name: ToDiscreteTimeModel
tools.description: Converts a continuous-time system model into a discrete-time model with a given sampling period. Discretization methods include zero-order hold, Tustin and matched pole-zero. Use it before implementing a controller in software.

tools.name: ToContinuousTimeModel
tools.description: Converts a discrete-time model back to continuous time, inverting the discretization. It is used when a system identified from sampled data must be analyzed in continuous time. The method should match the one used for discretization.

tools.name: TransferFunctionExpand
tools.description: Expands and simplifies the symbolic expression of a transfer function model while keeping it a model object. It is useful after algebraic interconnection, which often leaves unsimplified forms. Use it before reading off poles and zeros by hand.

tools.name: TransferFunctionTransform
tools.description: Applies a variable transformation to a transfer function, which implements frequency transformations such as lowpass to highpass or bandpass. It is central to analog filter design from prototypes. The transformation is given as a function of the complex variable.

tools.name: SystemsModelDelay
tools.description: Represents a pure time delay within a systems model, allowing delayed plants to be analyzed and simulated. Delays change phase without changing magnitude and limit achievable bandwidth. Use it to model transport lag and communication latency.

tools.name: SystemModel
tools.description: Represents a Modelica-based system model from the built-in library or a user model file, covering multi-domain physical systems. It exposes parameters, variables, equations and diagrams. Use it for acausal physical modelling of mechanical, electrical, thermal and hydraulic systems.
tools.notes: The built-in library covers Modelica standard components; Wolfram System Modeler provides a graphical editor for the same models.

tools.name: SystemModelSimulate
tools.description: Simulates a SystemModel over a time range, returning a SystemModelSimulationData object that can be queried for any variable. Parameter values and initial conditions can be overridden in the call. Use it to run physical system experiments numerically.

tools.name: SystemModelPlot
tools.description: Plots the results of a system model simulation, selecting variables by name. It handles axis labelling and units automatically. Use it as the standard visualization step after SystemModelSimulate.
tools.notes: SystemModelParametricSimulate builds a reusable function of the model parameters for sweeps and optimization.

tools.name: SystemModelLinearize
tools.description: Linearizes a nonlinear Modelica system model about an operating point, returning an AffineStateSpaceModel or StateSpaceModel. This bridges physical modelling and linear control design. Use it to design controllers for detailed physical plants.

tools.name: SystemModelParametricSimulate
tools.description: Creates a function that simulates a system model for given parameter values, so parameter sweeps and optimization can be run efficiently. The model is compiled once and reused. Use it for design-space exploration and calibration.

tools.name: AsymptoticOutputTracker
tools.description: Designs a controller that makes a nonlinear system's output asymptotically track a reference signal, using feedback linearization techniques. It returns the control law and the closed-loop system. Use it for nonlinear tracking problems where linear design is inadequate.

tools.name: SystemsModelExtract
tools.description: Extracts a subsystem from a multi-input multi-output model by selecting specific inputs and outputs. The result is a smaller model with the same dynamics restricted to those channels. Use it to analyze individual loops of a MIMO plant.

tools.name: SystemsModelMerge
tools.description: Combines several models into one larger model with stacked inputs and outputs. It is used to assemble multi-channel plants from individual channel models. The result behaves as a single MIMO system.
